Michelle Coghlan's scholarly analysis identifies a modern-Paris frame with an unnamed American narrator, followed by the Galliez report and historical material that the frame narrator recasts and expands; this establishes the frame/body division corroborated by the first- and third-person quotes.

person_note: The novel has a sustained first-person modern frame, directly exposed by q00004's narratorial speech beat, and a much longer historical body narrated in third person, locally exposed by q00005. Scholarly and reputable review evidence confirms that the unnamed American discovers the Galliez manuscript and then recasts it as the main historical narrative. The gnomic, rhetorical, and spoken pronouns in the other quotes are not additional narrative strands. Because different persons govern the frame and story sections, the appropriate book-level label is ALTERNATING; the main residual limitation is the absence of an accessible authorized continuous excerpt, but the quote evidence and Tier B structural analysis independently agree.
